desc: Ideation: per-bit GF(2) decomposition + parity DSU + per-component orientation flip for min sum
Implement full Python solution per plan (iterative find, union-by-size, flip rule, fast I/O)
Verify union parity sign on 2-node and 3-node chain cases; test self-loops, M=0, maxZ=0, contradictory triangle (sample 2), and samples 1 & 3
Confirm complexity/memory fit (≤30 bits × (N+M) DSU ops, ~1–2 s in Python) and finalize output formatting

**Union parity sign**: For edge `(x,y,w)`, we need `bit(x)^bit(y)=w`. With `bit(x)=diff[x]^bit(rx)`, `bit(y)=diff[y]^bit(ry)`, linking requires `bit(rx)^bit(ry) = w^diff[x]^diff[y] = t`. Attaching root `rx` under `ry` sets `diff[rx]=t`, which is exactly `bit(rx)^bit(ry)`. ✓ (Checked on 2-node and chain cases.)
**Iterative find**: collects path to root, then walks root-down accumulating `acc ^= diff[node]`, so each `diff[node]` becomes XOR-to-root and `parent[node]=root`. ✓
**Consistency check**: same-root case requires `diff[x]^diff[y]==w`; catches self-loops with `w=1` and contradictory duplicates (sample 2 triangle → `-1`). ✓

**Minimization**: the counting pass compresses every node, so `parent[v]` is the root when tallying `ones` and applying `flip`. Flip iff `ones*2 > size` (ties irrelevant). Each bit's one-count is independently minimized, and bits above `max_z.bit_length()` are optimally 0. ✓
**Edge cases**: `M=0` or `max_z=0` → `B=0` → all-zeros output (always consistent since all `w=0`). ✓
**Sample trace (Sample 1)**: bits 0,1 give `diff=[0,1,0]` (no flip, ones=1≤1), bit 2 gives `diff=[0,0,1]` → output `0 3 4`. ✓ Sample 2 conflicts at bit 1 → `-1`. ✓
**Complexity**: ≤30 bit-passes × O((N+M)·α) ≈ 9·10⁶ DSU operations with inlined finds and fast buffered I/O — fits comfortably.
